correctness.rationale: Fix an agent and measure all bundle values by their strictly positive tiers L<H. For s≥H and m<2n, every benchmark partition has an at-most-singleton part of value at most H≤s. For s<H, the agent's own bundle has t low goods, s=tL, and each of the p high goods must be alone in a foreign bundle: delete any other good to contradict EFX otherwise. Thus p≤n-1. After reserving those p bundles there are at most t+(n-p-1)(t+1) total low goods, since deletion of a low good from any other nonempty low bundle leaves at most t low goods. In any benchmark partition with all values strictly above s there would be at least n-p high-free parts, needing at least (n-p)(t+1) low goods, one more than available. This independent argument covers real tiers, empty bundles including m=0, and the case where a tier is absent. At m=2n the identical-valuations witness gives the focal recipient 4 from its two 2-goods, with every reduced foreign bundle worth at most 3 to any agent, so all EFX inequalities hold. Pair each 2 with a 3 to attain minimum 5 in the benchmark; the construction also works when n=2. In fact 5 is exact here: to beat 5 every part needs at least two goods, hence exactly two each, and a part containing a 2 cannot beat 5. The mathematical count, not the frozen finite integer-grid tests, proves both unrestricted quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The new content is the exact guarantee for every complete EFX allocation below 2n goods and the focal high-tier barrier without a supply bound. Prior positive bivalued counterexamples already show failure at equality for two agents, and padding with high pairs readily adapts the obstruction. The inspected exact MMS existence theorems do not imply the universal benchmark guarantee, and the inspected EFX guarantees are weaker. No inspected prior result covers the two positive statements.
residual_risks: Search and targeted full-text inspection are bounded; specialized uninspected EFX/MMS results could still overlap.

value.rationale: A sharp compatibility regime for two central fairness criteria gives useful information about all algorithmic outputs that are complete EFX under arbitrary personalized tiers, not just existence of a good output. The high-tier barrier is an agent-level sufficient criterion at any supply and shows why the ordinary singleton pigeonhole observation does not alone give this theorem. The statement validates exactly when the size-based guarantee first can fail without treating older counterexamples as new.
